item.title: Self-Hosted SPICE Circuit Simulation: ngspice vs Qucs vs Xyce for Electronics Design
item.description:
Why Self-Host Your Circuit Simulation?

Electronics design has traditionally relied on expensive commercial EDA suites like Cadence Virtuoso, Synopsys HSPICE, and Keysight ADS — tools that cost thousands of dollars per seat annually. Open-source SPICE simulators have matured to the point where they can handle professional-grade analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuit analysis without the licensing burden.

item.title: Open-Source FPGA Development Toolchain: Yosys vs Icarus Verilog vs GHDL vs nextpnr
item.description:
Introduction

Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) have traditionally been locked behind expensive proprietary toolchains from Xilinx (Vivado), Intel (Quartus), and Lattice (Diamond). A single Vivado license costs thousands of dollars per year, and the closed-source nature of these tools makes them difficult to integrate into automated CI/CD pipelines. The open-source FPGA toolchain — Yosys for synthesis, nextpnr for place-and-route, and Icarus Verilog or GHDL for simulation — has matured to the point where commercial FPGA designs can be developed entirely with free software.
